title: [contract] Reject duplicate active serial hashes per issuer
body:
## Context

`issue_claim` stores `serial_hash` on the claim but never checks whether the same issuer already has an **active** claim for that serial. An honest merchant can accidentally issue two deposits against one physical item; only one claim can be closed by a return scan, so the second deposit is stranded. A dishonest issuer can also inflate apparent claims for one item.

## What to do

- Add a per-issuer serial index, e.g. `DataKey::Serial(Address, BytesN<32>) -> u64`.
- In `issue_claim`, reject the call when an active claim already exists for `(issuer, serial_hash)`. Do this **before** the token transfer so no deposit moves and no claim id is consumed.
- Remove the index entry when the claim is redeemed (after the status change; the transaction reverts on failure).
- Transfers must keep the index entry. Suspending a merchant must not remove it.
- Add a new error variant (for example `SerialAlreadyActive`) and document it in `docs/LIFECYCLE.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Duplicate active serial for the same issuer fails with the new error.
- [ ] The failed call does not transfer tokens and does not increment `ClaimCount`.
- [ ] A different issuer can use the same serial hash.
- [ ] After redemption, the same serial can be issued again.
- [ ] Transferring a claim does not free the serial.
- [ ] `cargo test`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

## Files

- `contracts/looptag/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/looptag/src/test.rs`
- `docs/LIFECYCLE.md`

## Why this matters

The deposit is real money. A duplicate claim is an accounting bug even when nobody is malicious.

title: [contract][security] Guard against fee-on-transfer and non-standard SEP-41 tokens
body:
## Context

`issue_claim` records `deposit` and assumes the token transfer delivered exactly that amount. If a token deducts a fee or reports success without moving the full amount, the contract becomes undercollateralised: the claim promises more than the contract holds. The same assumption exists in `redeem`.

Stellar's native SAC behaves correctly, but the contract is designed to accept any SEP-41 asset. The trust model currently says "a correctly behaving token" without enforcing it.

## What to do

- Read the contract's token balance before and after the transfer in `issue_claim`.
- Require `after - before == deposit`; otherwise return a new `UnexpectedTransferAmount` error (transaction reverts).
- In `redeem`, require `before - after == claim.deposit`.
- Avoid introducing a second transfer or an unsafe re-entrancy window.
- Document the check in `docs/TRUST_MODEL.md` and add the error to `docs/LIFECYCLE.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A mock SEP-41 token that transfers less than requested causes `issue_claim` to fail.
- [ ] A mock token that burns or withholds part of the refund causes `redeem` to fail.
- [ ] The normal XLM SAC path still passes all existing tests.
- [ ] The check does not break fee-free tokens with 0 or non-7 decimals.
- [ ] Tests cover both failure modes and the happy path.

## Files

- `contracts/looptag/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/looptag/src/test.rs`
- `docs/TRUST_MODEL.md`, `docs/LIFECYCLE.md`

## Notes

A malicious token can still lie about `balance`; the goal is to catch accidental or naive fee-on-transfer behaviour, not to make arbitrary tokens safe. State that limit in the docs.

title: [contract] Add an admin pause that never blocks redemption
body:
## Context

There is no global circuit breaker. If a bug or exploit is found, the admin can only suspend merchants one at a time. A pause is useful for incident response, but a badly designed pause can strand customer deposits, which is worse than the bug.

## What to do

- Add an instance flag `Paused` and admin-only `pause` / `unpause` entry points.
- When paused: block `issue_claim`, `transfer_claim`, `authorize_return`, `register_merchant`, `register_station`, and `remove_station`.
- **Always allow** `redeem` and all read-only views. A customer must be able to recover a deposit that was already attested.
- Emit a typed `PauseChanged` event with the admin, new state, and ledger timestamp.
- Document the pause policy in `docs/TRUST_MODEL.md` and the error in `docs/LIFECYCLE.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Only the admin can pause or unpause.
- [ ] Paused state blocks new issuance, transfers, and return attestations.
- [ ] A claim already in `ReturnAuthorized` can still be redeemed while paused.
- [ ] Reads work while paused.
- [ ] Unpause restores normal operation.
- [ ] Tests cover each blocked path and every allowed path.

## Files

- `contracts/looptag/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/looptag/src/test.rs`
- `docs/LIFECYCLE.md`, `docs/TRUST_MODEL.md`

## Design note

Do not add a pause that allows the admin to move deposits. The pause must be a denial-of-service switch, not a custody switch.

title: [contract] Add two-step admin rotation
body:
## Context

The admin address is set once in `initialize` and can never change. A lost or compromised admin key permanently blocks merchant/station management. A one-step `set_admin` is risky because a typo can brick the contract.

## What to do

- Add `propose_admin(new_admin)` callable by the current admin. Store a pending admin and emit `AdminTransferProposed`.
- Add `accept_admin()` callable by the pending admin. Move `Admin` to the caller and clear the pending value; emit `AdminChanged`.
- Add `cancel_admin_transfer()` callable by the current admin.
- Add a read-only `get_pending_admin()`.
- Reject a proposal to the current admin or to an uninitialised state.
- Document the flow in `docs/LIFECYCLE.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Current admin can propose; the proposed address cannot act until it accepts.
- [ ] Only the pending admin can accept.
- [ ] The old admin loses admin rights after acceptance.
- [ ] Cancel works and leaves the current admin unchanged.
- [ ] Existing merchant/station/claim behaviour is unaffected.
- [ ] Tests cover unauthorised propose/accept/cancel and the full happy path.

## Files

- `contracts/looptag/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/looptag/src/test.rs`
- `docs/LIFECYCLE.md`

title: [contract][test] Add multi-merchant and station-revocation integration tests
body:
## Context

The current suite has 15 focused tests, but most accounting coverage is single-merchant. Two risks are not exercised end to end:

1. Two merchants with independent liabilities, including the same serial hash.
2. Revoking a station before versus after a return attestation.

## What to do

Add integration-style tests using the existing `Fixture`:

- Register merchants A and B; issue claims for both; assert `get_outstanding_liability` is independent.
- Let both merchants use the same serial hash; assert no cross-merchant collision.
- Redeem one claim and assert only that merchant's liability changes.
- Revoke a station before attestation → `authorize_return` fails.
- Attest a return, then revoke the station → `redeem` still succeeds.
- Suspend merchant A; assert merchant B can still issue and redeem.
- Assert the contract token balance equals the sum of both merchants' outstanding liabilities.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All scenarios above are covered by named tests.
- [ ] Existing tests still pass.
- [ ] No production code change is required unless a test exposes a real bug.
- [ ] If a bug is found, link the fix in the PR description.

## Files

- `contracts/looptag/src/test.rs`

## Why this matters

Accounting bugs often appear only when more than one issuer is involved.

title: [contract][test] Property-test the deposit accounting invariant
body:
## Context

The core invariant is:

```text
merchant.outstanding == Σ deposit of claims in {Active, ReturnAuthorized}
contract token balance  == Σ outstanding across all merchants
```

Unit tests check a few hand-written paths. A random lifecycle sequence is much better at finding double-counting, missed decrements, and id collisions.

## What to do

- Add a property-style test (for example with `proptest`, or a deterministic seeded generator if adding a dependency is undesirable).
- Generate sequences of: register merchant, issue claim, transfer, authorize return, redeem, suspend/reactivate.
- For each step, assert the contract balance and `Merchant.outstanding` against a model computed from the generated operations.
- Assert no claim can be transferred after `ReturnAuthorized` and no claim can be redeemed twice.
- Keep the test runtime reasonable (a few seconds, bounded operations).
- Add the invariant to `CONTRIBUTING.md` if it is not already there.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At least 100 generated sequences run in CI.
- [ ] Failing cases shrink to a readable minimal sequence.
- [ ] The test fails if `redeem` forgets to decrement `outstanding` (verify locally by temporarily breaking it).
- [ ] Runtime is bounded and documented.

## Files

- `contracts/looptag/Cargo.toml` (if a dev-dependency is added)
- `contracts/looptag/src/test.rs` or a new `tests/property.rs`

## Notes

Do not use `rand` without a fixed seed in CI; failures must be reproducible.

title: [sdk] Add transaction helpers for issue, transfer, return, and redeem
body:
## Context

The SDK exposes the generated client, but callers must know which arguments to validate, how to convert a serial hash to `Buffer`, and how to interpret the generated `Result<T>` values. That is enough rope to build an invalid transaction or misread an error.

## What to do

Add `packages/sdk/src/tx.ts` with typed helpers:

- `issueClaim(client, { issuer, owner, serial, deposit, expiresAt })`
- `transferClaim(client, { claimId, from, to })`
- `authorizeReturn(client, { claimId, station, serial })`
- `redeem(client, { claimId })`

Each helper should:

- Validate and normalise arguments (account ids, positive deposit, serial hash).
- Hash the serial with `hashSerial` and pass a `Buffer` to the generated client.
- Return the `AssembledTransaction` so the caller can `signAndSend`.
- Decode a failed simulation `Result` into a typed `LooptagError` with the numeric contract error code.
- Document the sign/send flow in the SDK README or root README.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Invalid addresses, zero/negative deposits, malformed serials, and unknown claim ids fail before a network call.
- [ ] A successful simulation returns the generated transaction object unchanged.
- [ ] Contract error codes 1–15 map to readable names/messages.
- [ ] Unit tests cover validation and error decoding without contacting testnet.
- [ ] README shows a full simulate → sign → send example.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @looptag/sdk build test typecheck` passes.

## Files

- `packages/sdk/src/tx.ts`, `packages/sdk/src/index.ts`
- `packages/sdk/test/tx.test.ts`
- `README.md`

## Notes

Do not sign or submit inside the helper. Keep key custody and wallet UX outside the SDK.

title: [sdk] Add an event poller with cursor and ledger-range handling
body:
## Context

`decodeLooptagEvent` can decode one event, but there is no supported way to fetch events from Soroban RPC, paginate, or resume after a restart. Every indexer/dashboard would reimplement this and get the cursor semantics subtly wrong.

## What to do

Add `packages/sdk/src/events-poller.ts` (or similar):

- `fetchLooptagEvents({ rpcUrl, contractId, startLedger, cursor, limit })`
- Call Soroban RPC `getEvents` with a contract filter and the `looptag` topic prefix if appropriate.
- Decode each event with `decodeLooptagEvent`; drop `null` events.
- Return `{ events, cursor, latestLedger, hasMore }`.
- Handle RPC errors and malformed event payloads without throwing away the rest of the page.
- Document cursor persistence and replay/idempotency expectations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A mocked RPC response returns decoded, typed events.
- [ ] Unknown events are ignored, not fatal.
- [ ] Cursor and latest ledger are propagated correctly.
- [ ] A malformed event is skipped and reported in a `skipped` count or warning.
- [ ] Tests cover first page, next page, and RPC failure.
- [ ] No network calls in unit tests.

## Files

- `packages/sdk/src/events-poller.ts`, `packages/sdk/src/index.ts`
- `packages/sdk/test/events-poller.test.ts`
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` if the flow needs a diagram

## Why this matters

Without a cursor, an indexer either misses events or replays the entire chain on every start.

title: [sdk][good first] Add Stellar account and network validation helpers
body:
## Context

`qr.ts` validates contract ids, but the SDK does not validate account ids or network names. The future transaction helpers will need both, and callers currently have to import `StrKey` themselves.

## What to do

- Add `isValidAccountId(value: string): boolean` using `StrKey.isValidEd25519PublicKey` (and, if useful, `isValidMuxedAccount` with a clear name).
- Add `assertNetwork(network)` for the same `testnet | mainnet | futurenet | local` union used by the QR module.
- Add `networkPassphrase(network)` returning the correct SDF passphrase, with `local` requiring an explicit override rather than guessing.
- Export the helpers from `src/index.ts`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Valid testnet/mainnet account ids return `true`; contract ids and random strings return `false`.
- [ ] Unknown network names throw a descriptive error.
- [ ] Testnet and mainnet passphrases are correct; `local` behaviour is documented.
- [ ] Vitest covers valid, invalid, and edge cases (empty string, 55/57 chars).

## Files

- `packages/sdk/src/network.ts` (new) or `src/qr.ts`
- `packages/sdk/src/index.ts`
- `packages/sdk/test/network.test.ts`

## Good first issue

This is self-contained, has no network dependency, and only touches the SDK.

title: [sdk][good first] Reject ambiguous numeric amounts in money parsing
body:
## Context

`toBaseUnits` accepts `string | number`. Strings are exact. Numbers are not: JavaScript converts small values to exponent notation, and `numberToPlainString` currently falls back to `toFixed(7)`, which can silently round a value such as `1.23e-7` to `0.0000001`.

Passing a float to a money API is already a smell, but silently rounding is worse than rejecting.

## What to do

- Detect exponent-notation numbers that cannot be represented exactly at the requested decimals.
- Reject them with a clear error telling the caller to pass a decimal string.
- Keep exact integer and simple decimal numbers working.
- Add a README/JSDoc note that money should be passed as a string.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `toStroops("1.23e-7")` as a string still fails the plain-decimal regex.
- [ ] `toStroops(1.23e-7)` (number) throws instead of rounding.
- [ ] `toStroops(0.0000001)` and `toStroops(2)` still work.
- [ ] Tests cover `1e-7`, `1.23e-7`, `1e21`, `NaN`, and `Infinity`.
- [ ] Existing amount tests pass unchanged.

## Files

- `packages/sdk/src/amount.ts`
- `packages/sdk/test/amount.test.ts`
- `README.md` (short note)

## Good first issue

Focused change with an obvious failing test.

title: [sdk] Add a QR payload builder from an on-chain claim
body:
## Context

Callers building a QR payload must manually combine the network, contract id, claim id, and serial hash. A mismatch between the hash printed on the tag and the hash stored on-chain silently produces a tag that can never be returned.

## What to do

- Add `claimToQrPayload(claim, { network, contractId, serialHash })` that:
  - Verifies `serialHash` equals `claim.serial_hash` (hex, case-insensitive) and throws if not.
  - Derives `claimId` from `claim.id`.
  - Validates `contractId` and `network` using the existing QR rules.
- Add `encodeClaimQrFromClaim(claim, options)` as a convenience wrapper.
- Add a `serialHashToBuffer` helper for transaction helpers.
- Document the builder in `docs/QR_FORMAT.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Correct claim/hash produces the same payload as `encodeClaimQr`.
- [ ] A mismatched hash throws before producing a QR string.
- [ ] Uppercase hex is normalised to lowercase.
- [ ] A malformed claim id (0, > u64 max) throws.
- [ ] Tests cover happy path and each rejection.

## Files

- `packages/sdk/src/qr.ts`
- `packages/sdk/test/qr.test.ts`
- `docs/QR_FORMAT.md`

title: [indexer] Build a minimal read-only indexer and REST API
body:
## Context

There is no backend. The demo reads a committed snapshot, and any merchant dashboard would need to scan events from scratch. A small read-only indexer makes the data usable without giving it custody of funds.

## What to do

Create `packages/indexer` (Node + TypeScript):

- Poll contract events from Soroban RPC using the SDK event helpers.
- Persist claims, merchants, stations, and a cursor. SQLite (`better-sqlite3`) or a JSON file with atomic writes is acceptable; choose one and justify it.
- Idempotent upserts so replaying a ledger range is safe.
- HTTP endpoints:
  - `GET /health`
  - `GET /claims/:id`
  - `GET /owners/:address/claims`
  - `GET /merchants/:address`
- A `GET /claims?status=active&limit=50&cursor=...` list endpoint.
- Config via environment variables; no secrets committed.
- Unit tests for decoding/upsert logic with a mocked RPC page.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Indexer restarts without losing its cursor.
- [ ] Replaying the same page does not duplicate rows.
- [ ] Unknown events are ignored.
- [ ] API validates addresses/ids and returns useful 4xx errors.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @looptag/indexer build test` passes.
- [ ] README documents run and testnet sync commands.

## Files

- `packages/indexer/**`
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (already includes `packages/*`)
- root scripts / README

## Notes

Keep it read-only. No private keys, no transaction signing, no custody.

title: [demo] Add a wallet-connected transfer and redeem flow
body:
## Context

The demo is a read-only snapshot. The most important user action — taking a claim and redeeming it — cannot be tried. A wallet-connected flow is the difference between a screenshot and a usable prototype.

## What to do

- Add a demo page (or section) that connects a Stellar wallet (Freighter or Stellar Wallets Kit).
- Load claim #1 (or an id from the URL) from testnet via the SDK.
- If the connected account owns an `Active` claim, offer **Transfer**; if it owns a `ReturnAuthorized` claim, offer **Redeem**.
- Simulate, show the expected result/fee, then sign and submit. Display the transaction hash and a Stellar Expert link.
- Handle: wallet not installed, user rejection, wrong network, insufficient fee, simulation error, stale claim.
- Clearly label testnet-only and never ask for a secret key.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can connect a testnet wallet and see their address.
- [ ] Transfer and redeem build real transactions; no mocked success path.
- [ ] Wrong-network and rejected-signature states are handled without a broken UI.
- [ ] Every submitted transaction links to Stellar Expert.
- [ ] Manual test evidence is included in the PR.
- [ ] No secret key is ever read or stored.

## Files

- `demo/index.html`, `demo/app.js`, `demo/styles.css`
- `packages/sdk` if a helper is missing
- `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` for a manual test recipe

title: [demo] Add a station return scanner
body:
## Context

Return stations are half of the protocol, but there is no station tool. A station currently has to use the CLI and copy a serial hash by hand.

## What to do

- Add `demo/station.html` with a camera QR scanner and a paste-the-payload fallback.
- Decode the payload with `decodeClaimQr`; fetch the claim from testnet.
- Compare the QR's `serialHash` with the on-chain `claim.serial_hash` and show a clear match/mismatch state.
- Let the station connect a wallet, verify it is authorised (`is_station`), and submit `authorize_return`.
- Show the claim status transition and the transaction link.
- Handle denied camera permission and unsupported browsers gracefully.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A valid demo QR can be scanned or pasted and resolved to claim #1.
- [ ] A mismatched/corrupt payload is rejected before any transaction.
- [ ] The UI explains that the station must still read the physical serial; the QR alone is not proof.
- [ ] An unauthorised wallet gets a readable error, not a raw contract code.
- [ ] Manual test evidence is included in the PR.

## Files

- `demo/station.html`, shared JS/CSS
- `packages/sdk` scanner helper if needed
- `docs/QR_FORMAT.md`

title: [demo] Add a merchant liability dashboard and CSV export
body:
## Context

`Merchant` already tracks `issued`, `redeemed`, and `outstanding`, but there is no view for a merchant to see its liability or export it for accounting.

## What to do

- Add `demo/merchant.html` that takes a merchant address (or connects a wallet).
- Show: active claims, return-authorized claims, redeemed claims, total outstanding, issued/redeemed counts.
- List claims with id, owner, deposit, status, issued date, serial hash (truncated).
- Add a **Download CSV** button with stable columns and ISO timestamps.
- Use the indexer if available; otherwise document the RPC/event limitation and show the snapshot data.
- Include an empty state and a clear "testnet data" label.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dashboard renders the canonical merchant (`Circular Cafe`) from the manifest.
- [ ] CSV includes only the displayed merchant's claims and escapes fields correctly.
- [ ] Outstanding total matches `get_outstanding_liability`.
- [ ] Loading/error/empty states are handled.
- [ ] Screenshots or a short recording are included in the PR.

## Files

- `demo/merchant.html`, shared JS/CSS
- `packages/sdk` helpers if needed

title: [demo] Load live contract state from Soroban RPC with a staleness indicator
body:
## Context

The demo currently reads `deployments/testnet.json`, which is a snapshot. A visitor cannot tell whether the on-chain claim still matches the page, and after a new deployment the page can silently lie.

## What to do

- On load, fetch the claim and merchant from Soroban RPC via the SDK.
- Compare live values with the manifest; show a badge: `Live`, `Snapshot (RPC unavailable)`, or `Mismatch`.
- Show the latest ledger and the time of the last successful fetch.
- Add a retry button and a short timeout.
- Never fail the whole page if RPC is down; degrade to the snapshot with a visible warning.
- Keep the page dependency-free or use a pinned CDN build with a documented version.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With RPC available, the page shows live claim status/owner and latest ledger.
- [ ] With RPC blocked, the page still renders the snapshot and says so.
- [ ] A manifest/live mismatch is visible, not hidden.
- [ ] No secrets or write operations are involved.
- [ ] Manual test with devtools network throttling is included in the PR.

## Files

- `demo/index.html`, `demo/app.js`
- `packages/sdk/src/client.ts` if a read helper is needed

title: [ci] Enforce a contract WASM size budget and manifest hash check
body:
## Context

CI builds and tests the contract, but nothing stops a dependency or code change from bloating the WASM past a practical deployment budget. The deployment manifest also records a WASM hash that is never checked automatically.

## What to do

- Add `scripts/check-contract-size.mjs`:
  - Read the built `contracts/target/wasm32v1-none/release/looptag.wasm`.
  - Fail if size exceeds a documented budget (start at 32 KiB; the current build is ~14.8 KiB).
  - Print the size and SHA-256.
- Add an optional `--manifest` mode that compares the SHA-256 with `deployments/testnet.json` and warns/fails when `CHECK_DEPLOYED_HASH=1`.
- Wire the size check into CI after the release build.
- Document the budget in `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` and why it exists (ledger entry rent, deploy cost, reviewability).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CI fails if the WASM is missing or over budget.
- [ ] CI prints the hash so reviewers can compare it to the manifest.
- [ ] `pnpm check:contract` works locally.
- [ ] The hash check is opt-in for deployed manifests (toolchain differences should not break normal PRs).
- [ ] The budget is justified in docs.

## Files

- `scripts/check-contract-size.mjs`
- `package.json`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`

title: [docs][good first] Add a glossary and first-hour contributor walkthrough
body:
## Context

The docs are precise but dense for a first-time contributor. Terms like issuer, station, claim, deposit token, SAC, and liability are used before they are defined, and there is no single "do this first" path.

## What to do

- Add `docs/GLOSSARY.md` defining: claim, deposit, issuer/merchant, owner, station, serial hash, SAC, SEP-41, outstanding liability, return attestation, redemption, pause, TTL.
- Add a short `docs/FIRST_HOUR.md` walkthrough:
  1. Clone and install.
  2. Run SDK and contract tests.
  3. Read the lifecycle doc.
  4. Inspect claim #1 on Stellar Expert.
  5. Pick a `good first issue` and comment.
- Link both from `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every term used in the README/lifecycle has a glossary entry.
- [ ] The walkthrough commands work from a clean clone.
- [ ] No broken links (`pnpm check:docs`).
- [ ] Tone is direct and does not duplicate entire docs pages.

## Files

- `docs/GLOSSARY.md`, `docs/FIRST_HOUR.md`
- `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`

title: [docs] Add a pilot merchant runbook and incident response checklist
body:
## Context

The code explains the protocol, but not how to operate it. A pilot merchant needs to know how to choose stations, manage keys, respond to a stuck claim, and pause issuance without stranding deposits.

## What to do

Create `docs/RUNBOOK.md` covering:

- **Onboarding:** deploy, initialize, register merchant, choose stations, print tags.
- **Key management:** admin vs merchant vs station vs owner keys; testnet separation; rotation status (link the two-step admin issue).
- **Daily checks:** outstanding liability vs token balance, station liveness, stuck `ReturnAuthorized` claims.
- **Incident playbook:** suspected station collusion, compromised admin, RPC outage, contract bug, pause/unpause, customer communication.
- **Stuck claim:** what to do when a station refuses; escalation and evidence collection.
- **Shutdown:** stop issuance, redeem outstanding claims, revoke stations, archive evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Runbook is actionable, with commands and owner/role for each step.
- [ ] It never suggests moving customer deposits or using an admin backdoor.
- [ ] It links to threat model, lifecycle, and deployment docs.
- [ ] A reviewer can follow the daily checks against the canonical testnet deployment.
- [ ] `pnpm check:docs` passes.

## Files

- `docs/RUNBOOK.md`
- `README.md` (link)

title: [docs] Add a contract API reference and event catalog
body:
## Context

`LIFECYCLE.md` explains the flow, but there is no single reference for every function signature, auth requirement, return type, error, and event. SDK users and reviewers have to read Rust or the generated bindings.

## What to do

- Add `docs/API.md` with a table per entry point:
  - name, arguments and types, auth required, returns, errors, state change, event.
- Cover all public functions: `initialize`, `register_merchant`, `set_merchant_active`, `register_station`, `remove_station`, `issue_claim`, `transfer_claim`, `authorize_return`, `redeem`, and all read-only views.
- Add an event catalog with topic names and data fields, matching `packages/sdk/src/events.ts`.
- Add a short "how to regenerate the TypeScript bindings" link to `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`.
- Cross-check against `stellar contract spec` or the generated bindings; note any mismatch as a bug.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every public contract function is documented.
- [ ] Every event emitted in `lib.rs` appears in the catalog with its fields.
- [ ] Error codes 1–15 are listed or linked.
- [ ] The SDK event union and the catalog agree.
- [ ] `pnpm check:docs` passes.

## Files

- `docs/API.md`
- `README.md`, `docs/LIFECYCLE.md` (links)

## Notes

Prefer a generated spec plus a hand-written explanation over duplicating the Rust doc comments verbatim.

title: [sdk][good first] Add tests for client explorer helpers and merchant lifecycle events
body:
## Context

`client.ts` exposes `explorerTxUrl` and `explorerContractUrl`, and `events.ts` decodes `merchant_status_changed` and `claim_transferred`, but those paths have no direct tests. A small regression here breaks every dashboard link or silently drops an event.

## What to do

- Add `packages/sdk/test/client.test.ts`:
  - Valid tx hash produces the expected Stellar Expert URL.
  - Default contract URL uses the generated testnet contract id.
  - An explicit contract id overrides the default.
- Extend `packages/sdk/test/events.test.ts`:
  - Decode `merchant_status_changed` (name, active).
  - Decode `claim_transferred` (claim id, from, to).
- Keep the tests pure; no network calls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New tests fail if the URL path or event field mapping changes.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @looptag/sdk test` passes.
- [ ] No production code change unless a test exposes a real bug (then describe it).

## Files

- `packages/sdk/test/client.test.ts` (new)
- `packages/sdk/test/events.test.ts`

## Good first issue

Two small test files, no architecture decisions.

title: [contract] Add a bounded batch claim view for dashboards
body:
## Context

A merchant dashboard or wallet that owns many claims has to make one RPC simulation per claim. That is slow and can hit rate limits. A bounded batch read is a small, safe improvement.

## What to do

- Add `get_claims(env, claim_ids: Vec<u64>) -> Result<Vec<Claim>, Error>`.
- Enforce a maximum batch size (for example 50) with a new `BatchTooLarge` error. This bounds CPU and ledger read cost.
- Preserve input order. If any id is missing, return `ClaimNotFound` (or document a different policy and test it).
- Bump each returned claim's TTL exactly as `get_claim` does.
- Do not add a storage index; this is a read helper, not a new source of truth.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Batch of 1, 50, and 51 ids behaves as documented.
- [ ] Output order matches input order.
- [ ] Missing id returns the documented error and does not panic.
- [ ] TTL bump is applied to every returned claim.
- [ ] Existing views and tests are unaffected.
- [ ] `docs/API.md` (or `LIFECYCLE.md`) documents the limit.

## Files

- `contracts/looptag/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/looptag/src/test.rs`
- `docs/API.md` / `docs/LIFECYCLE.md`

## Notes

Do not make the batch unbounded. Soroban charges for CPU and ledger reads; an unbounded vector is a denial-of-service footgun.
